title: Simple vs compound interest: why compound grows faster
examples: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
Why does compound interest grow faster?
How much is 1000 after 3 years at 10% compound interest?

explain.say: You put 1,000 rupees in a bank that pays 10 percent interest a year. Interest is extra money the bank pays you for keeping your money there. Look at the first bar: 1,000 rupees to start.

draw.text: Simple vs compound interest: why compound grows faster

explain.say: With simple interest, you get 10 percent of the first 1,000 every year. That is 100 rupees each year. After 3 years: 1,300. See the bars grow by the same step each time?
With compound interest, you also earn interest on your interest. Year 1: 1,100. Year 2: 10 percent of 1,100 is 110, so 1,210. What do you think year 3 will be?
1,331! Compound interest grows like a snowball rolling downhill: the bigger it gets, the faster it grows. On a graph it curves upward, while simple interest is a straight line.

marks.label: Compound snowball
marks.ask: Why does compound interest grow faster?

explain.say: Fantastic! After 3 years the gap is only 31 rupees. But after 30 years, compound gives about 17,449 rupees, and simple only 4,000! Challenge: what single number do you multiply by each year for 10 percent compound interest?

faq.a: Interest is money paid for using money. A bank pays you interest on savings, and you pay interest when you borrow.
Interest worked out on the starting amount only, so you get the same amount every year. 10 percent of 1,000 is 100 rupees a year.
asks: How do you calculate simple interest?

faq.a: Interest added to your money each year, so next year you earn interest on the interest too. Multiply by 1.1 each year for 10 percent.
asks: How do you calculate compound interest?

faq.q: Why does compound interest grow faster?
faq.a: Each year the interest is worked out on a bigger amount, so the yearly interest keeps growing: 100, then 110, then 121.
asks: Why is compound interest better for savings?

faq.q: What is the formula for compound interest?
faq.a: Amount equals the starting amount times the multiplier to the power of the number of years. 1,000 times 1.1 to the power 3 is 1,331.

facts: 1,000 at 10% compound interest for 3 years grows to 1,000 × 1.1³ = 1,331.
After 30 years at 10%, compound interest turns 1,000 into about 17,449, while simple interest gives 4,000.

quiz.say: You save 500 dollars at 4 percent simple interest. How much interest do you get in 3 years?
quiz.why: 4 percent of 500 is 20 dollars a year, and 3 years gives 60 dollars.

wrong.1: 20 dollars is just one year of interest.
wrong.2: 560 dollars is the total in the account, not the interest.

quiz.say: 1,000 rupees earns 10 percent compound interest. How much is there after 2 years?

wrong.1: 1,200 is simple interest, which ignores interest on interest.
